title: fix(tests): gate the unit project's shared-global invariant, and stop the fetch leak that breaks the network-escape ledger
body:
Fixes #8500

## The defect, re-measured on today's tree

`origin/main` `c30026715`, dedicated worktree, fresh install, nothing else:

```
pnpm exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2
  Test Files  1 failed | 977 passed (978)
       Tests  1 failed | 16666 passed | 2 skipped (16669)
 FAIL scripts/__tests__/network-escape-ledger.test.ts
   > still wraps the global fetch to record escapes
 AssertionError: expected 'Mock' to be 'guardedFetch'
```

The card's premise holds: the failure still reproduces, and the writer is real.

## What was actually leaking

The `unit` project runs `isolate: false` — one module graph and one global object per worker. `vitest.config.mts` already writes out the first invariant that pays for that (ComponentRegistry keys) and hands enforcement to `scripts/__tests__/unit-registry-absence-collision.test.ts`. `globalThis` is the second invariant of the same class, and it had no gate:

> a global the setup files install must be the same value at the END of a file as it was at the START of it.

Five files broke it. Four replaced `globalThis.fetch` with a bare `vi.fn()` by assignment; one left a `vi.stubGlobal('localStorage', ...)` standing, which under `isolate: false` is undone by whichever LATER file calls `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` first, restoring a value that file never installed.

- `packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/ActionRunner.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/ActionRunner.bodyExtra.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/ActionRunner.bodyShape.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/UndoManager.test.ts`
- `packages/app-shell/src/preview/__tests__/commitHistory.test.ts`

A bare assignment is undone by neither `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` nor `vi.restoreAllMocks()`, because neither knows the value was ever replaced. That is why `commitHistory.test.ts`, which already called `vi.restoreAllMocks()` in an `afterEach`, still leaked.

## Direction 1, both halves — as the triage seat's routing opinion asked

**The writers hand the global back.** `vi.stubGlobal` in, `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` out.

**The next writer is caught, not discovered.** `vitest.setup.shared-global-leak-guard.ts` arms a per-file `afterAll` in every `isolate: false` project. It snapshots what the setup files installed, reds the file that left one replaced, and — before it throws — puts the value back, so the file that leaked is the only one that goes red instead of the failure surfacing three files later in one that did nothing wrong.

It has to be a setup file, and that is measured rather than stylistic. Vitest re-executes `setupFiles` for every test file even under `isolate: false`, while a module those setup files *import* is evaluated once per worker — so a hook registered in such a module attaches to the first test file of the worker and to no other:

```
ZZPROBE inner body ran, count= 1     <- module imported BY a setup file
ZZPROBE setup body ran, count= 1     <- the setup file itself
ZZPROBE afterEach n= 1               <- setup file's hook, file 1
ZZPROBE inner afterEach n= 1         <- imported module's hook, file 1
ZZPROBE setup body ran, count= 2     <- setup file re-executes for file 2
ZZPROBE afterEach n= 2               <- its hook fires again
                                     <- the imported module's hook does NOT
```

`afterAll` and not `afterEach`, because the invariant is about what crosses a FILE boundary: the network-escape guard's own `Fix:` text prescribes leaving a module-scope double up for a whole file when the component can read after the test body returns, and an `afterEach` here would red exactly that prescribed shape.

The guard is wired only into projects that set `isolate: false`. `dom` / `dom-heavy` / `dist` keep `isolate: true`, where each file gets its own global object and nothing crosses.

## A second leak the new guard found immediately

`scripts/__tests__/unit-registry-absence-collision.test.ts` imports the project's closures into a private module graph after `vi.resetModules()`. One of the specifiers it resolves is `vitest.setup.network-escape-guard` — `scripts/__tests__/network-escape-ledger.test.ts` imports it by path — so the guard RE-EXECUTED there and installed a second `guardedFetch` over the first. Both wrappers are named `guardedFetch`, so the ledger test could never see the swap, and every file after that one in the worker ran with a doubled wrapper whose `afterEach` belonged to a module instance the run had already discarded. That gate now snapshots and restores the globals around its measurement.

## Evidence

Full `unit` project, before and after, same worktree, both through the shared verify lock:

```
before  Test Files  1 failed | 977 passed (978)   Tests  1 failed | 16666 passed | 2 skipped
after   Test Files  979 passed (979)              Tests  16678 passed | 2 skipped (16680)
```

`@object-ui/console` project (it merges this config): 90 files / 1072 tests passed.

**Reverse verification 1 — the guard can fail.** The stub in `ActionRunner.bodyShape.test.ts` was reverted to the raw assignment on disk (`git hash-object` moved `fd231cdc` -> `8daf94e0`; the anchored marker counts inverted both ways: stub-form 1->0, raw-form 0->1, unstub 1->0), and the file alone was run:

```
Error: Shared-global leak: this test FILE left a global replaced.
  - globalThis.fetch: expected function guardedFetch, found function Mock
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The 7 tests of the file still pass; only the leak reds, and it reds on the writer. Restored under a trap and proved by state, not by an exit code: blob back to `fd231cdc`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

**Reverse verification 2 — the wiring pin is not vacuous.** The guard was removed from the `unit` project's `setupFiles` on disk (blob `37c1635d` -> `ce585009`; armed-count 2->1 while base-count held at 3), and `shared-global-leak-guard.test.ts` went red on exactly the two wiring assertions:

```
AssertionError: every `isolate: false` project must list
  vitest.setup.shared-global-leak-guard.ts in its setupFiles.
AssertionError: the guard is armed in a project that is not `isolate: false`.
 Test Files  1 failed (1)   Tests  2 failed | 9 passed (11)
```

Restored the same way: blob back to `37c1635d`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

Gates: `pnpm type-check:vitest-setup` exit 0 (after building the four packages its program resolves through), `pnpm type-check:scripts` exit 0, `turbo run type-check --filter @object-ui/core --filter @object-ui/app-shell` 31/31, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exit 0, `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` exit 0, `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` NOT GOVERNED.

ESLint, narrowed and declared: `pnpm lint:root` exit 0 (32 warnings, 0 errors) plus `turbo run lint --filter @object-ui/core --filter @object-ui/app-shell` 3/3 successful (2925 warnings, 0 errors), and `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 10 changed files, exit 0, 9 warnings and 0 errors — all pre-existing `no-explicit-any` on lines the diff did not touch. Type-aware linting is not enabled in `eslint.config.js` (no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not contain. Ratchet counts read on `51ee1fdff`. The repo-wide `eslint .` sweep is CI's.

## Filed, not fixed here

**objectui#8537** — the same guard file's OTHER half is inert: its `afterEach`, the one its header calls "the `afterEach` that fails ANY escape in ANY file", registers only for the first test file each worker runs in the `unit` project, by exactly the mechanism the probe above shows. Two byte-identical escaping files run together: only the first reds. Repairing it is a separate blast radius — escapes invisible today would all turn red at once, and how many there are has not been measured — so it is filed unlabelled for triage rather than ridden in here.

## Notes

- `Test (shard 2/4)` is flaky in this repository on `ObjectKanban.contractEnvelope-6839.test.tsx:134`, tracked as objectui#8493 and unrelated to this diff.
- The changeset declares an empty frontmatter: this is test infrastructure and releases nothing.
